rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the Qur'anic wording in 57:23 a more eloquent and concise expression than the preceding poetic line about worldly joy.
rows.anchor: لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بما ءاتاكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun's joy was shirk because it came without fear of God's punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان فرحه ذلك شركا

words: وَٱبْتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi takes Qarun to acknowledge the afterlife: use God's gift of wealth for what leads to Paradise, while adopting humility.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه كان مقرا بالآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reading is that Qarun was so absorbed in earning wealth that he neglected enjoyment, so the adviser told him to make time for it.
rows.anchor: لعله كان مستغرق الهم في طلب الدنيا فلأجل ذلك ما كان يتفرغ للتنعم والالتذاذ فنهاه الواعظ عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading permits enjoyment of lawful worldly pleasures alongside the call to spend wealth for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لما أمره الواعظ بصرف المال إلى الآخرة بين له بهذا الكلام أنه لا بأس بالتمتع بالوجوه المباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading makes spending in God's obedience one's true share of worldly life, unlike merely eating and drinking.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الإنفاق في طاعة الله فإن ذلك هو نصيب المرء من الدنيا دون الذي يأكل ويشرب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Razi quotes a prophetic exhortation to take from oneself for oneself, prepare in worldly life for the afterlife, and use youth and life before old age and death; after death only Paradise or Hell remains.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( فليأخذ العبد من نفسه لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command extends beyond financial giving to all kindness, including help through wealth or status, a cheerful face, a warm welcome, and favorable mention.
rows.anchor: بالإحسان بالمال أمره بالإحسان مطلقا ويدخل فيه الإعانة بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the reminder to reciprocate God's beneficence evokes the promise that gratitude brings increase.
rows.anchor: لئن شكرتم لازيدنكم } ( إبراهيم : 7 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The corruption forbidden here is the oppression and transgression Qarun practiced.
rows.anchor: والمراد ما كان عليه من الظلم والبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify Moses as the speaker of this admonition.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن هذا القائل هو موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpreters identify the speaker as the believers among Qarun's own people.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون بل مؤمنو قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says this admonition was already complete and could not be improved, yet Qarun refused it and answered with ingratitude by claiming his wealth came from his own knowledge.
rows.anchor: ما لو قيل لم يكن عليه مزيد

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Qatadah, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi say Qarun was Israel's foremost Torah scholar and claimed his learning and merit entitled him to the wealth.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي : كان قارون أقرأ بني إسرائيل للتوراة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Dahhak say Moses received alchemical knowledge from heaven and divided it among Qarun, Joshua, and Caleb; Qarun tricked the others, took their shares, and transmuted lead to silver and copper to gold.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك : كان موسى عليه السلام أنزل عليه علم الكيمياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes Qarun to mean that his expertise in commerce and methods of earning produced his wealth.
rows.anchor: أراد به علمه بوجوه المكاسب والتجارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reading says God gave Qarun wealth while knowing his circumstances, which he takes to prove it was good for him; عندي means 'in my view' or belief.
rows.anchor: الله أعطاني ذلك مع كونه عالما بي وبأحوالي

words: أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question may affirm Qarun knew from the Torah, Moses, and historical transmitters that God had destroyed stronger and richer peoples, yet he still boasted of his own resources.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا إثباتا لعلمه بأن الله تعالى قد أهلك قبله

words: أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question denies that Qarun possessed useful knowledge: he claimed knowledge made him deserve every blessing but lacked knowledge that could guard him from the fate of the destroyed.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون نفيا لعلمه بذلك كأنه لما قال أوتيته على علم عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جمعا may mean a greater accumulation of wealth or a larger gathering and number of people.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أكثر جمعا للمال أو أكثر جماعة وعددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is that Qarun's confidence in wealth, strength, and supporters was deeply mistaken: when God wills his destruction, none of these resources, however multiplied, can help.
rows.anchor: وحاصل الجواب أن اغتراره بماله وقوته وجموعه من الخطأ العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no inquiry into the nature or extent of criminals' sins when punishing them, because He already knows everything.
rows.anchor: لأنه تعالى عالم بكل المعلومات فلا حاجة به إلى السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reconciles this with the promise to question everyone in 15:92 by assigning the verses to two different times, as he explains elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قلنا يحمل ذلك على وقتين على ما قررناه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim distinguishes questioning for accounting, reproach, or seeking an opportunity to make amends; the last is most apt here, as other verses say disbelievers are denied it and cannot excuse themselves.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو مسلم وجها آخر فقال : السؤال قد يكون للمحاسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation connects the sinking directly to Qarun's arrogance, insolence, and excess; the verse's فاء signals this causal relation.
rows.anchor: لما أشر وبطر وعتا خسف الله به وبداره الأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Report says Qarun, angered by Moses's levy, bribed a woman to accuse him; she confessed, and Moses ordered earth to swallow Qarun and companions despite pleas. God rebuked him; Israelites suspected greed, and Qarun sinks a hundred qāma daily.
rows.anchor: قيل إن قارون كان يؤذي نبي الله موسى عليه السلام كل وقت وهو يداريه للقرابة التي بينهما حتى نزلت الزكاة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says Qarun's descent to the seventh earth or any lesser depth is not impossible if the report is understood as rhetorical exaggeration meant to deter.
rows.anchor: إذا هلك بالخسف فسواء نزل عن ظاهر الأرض إلى الأرض السابعة

words: فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةٍ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi finds it unlikely that God would have answered their pleas if they had called on Him, unless the plea included repentance: they persisted in wrongdoing, and Moses acted under God's command.
rows.anchor: فإن صح حمل على استغاثة مقرونة بالتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the claims that Qarun sinks endlessly and by a specified number of measures each day, since descent must have an end and the stated number is equally doubtful.
rows.anchor: وقولهم إنه يتجلجل في الأرض أبدا فبعيد لأنه لا بد له من نهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi considers these isolated, conflicting reports of little use and unable to establish certainty; since this is not a practical ruling, he prefers relying on the Qur'an and leaving further details to God.
rows.anchor: والذي عندي في أمثال هذه الحكايات أنها قليلة الفائدة لأنها من باب أخبار الآحاد فلا تفيد اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means Qarun could neither avenge himself on Moses nor fend off God's punishment; انتصر is to protect oneself from an adversary's aid or force.
rows.anchor: من المنتقمين من موسى أو من الممتنعين من عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun refers to Noah's ship, it was a sign because God guided its construction before the flood, made the water recede before provisions ran out, and protected it from violent winds and harmful creatures.
rows.anchor: أنها راجعة إلى السفينة المذكورة وعلى هذا ففي كونها آية وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to the event or to the deliverance, either of which God made a sign for all peoples.
rows.anchor: جعلنا الواقعة أو النجاة آية للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim is read in the accusative, the well-known reading, or in the nominative, meaning 'and among the messengers was Abraham.'
rows.anchor: وفي إبراهيم وجهان من القراءة أحدهما : النصب وهو المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the accusative, Ibrahim may be governed by an omitted 'remember,' or by the earlier 'We sent' in 29:14.
rows.anchor: أنه منصوب بفعل غير مذكور وهو معنى اذكر إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If 'when he said to his people' modifies 'We sent,' it seems to put the sending after the call even though sending normally precedes preaching; Razi offers two resolutions.
rows.anchor: أي أرسلنا إبراهيم إذ قال لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One resolution is that sending extends over time: Abraham remained a messenger while addressing his people, as standing can continue until a prince exits his house.
rows.anchor: أن الإرسال أمر يمتد فهو حال قوله لقومه اعبدوا الله كان مرسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abraham already recognized idolatry's error through God's guidance and called people to Islam before his formal sending; God sent him while he was preaching.
rows.anchor: هو أن إبراهيم بمجرد هداية الله إياه كان يعلم فساد قول المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes worship affirm God's existence and piety deny any other deity, since associating another with the sovereign is a grave offense.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى التوحيد لأن التوحيد إثبات الإله ونفي غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, worship means fulfilling obligations and fearing God means refraining from prohibitions; affirmation of God and avoiding shirk fall under these commands.
rows.anchor: الامتناع عن المحرمات ويدخل في الأول الاعتراف بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that reason requires a necessary existent as the cause of possible beings; denying God would leave existence without an ultimate cause and entail an impossible regress.
rows.anchor: أما عقلا فلأن الممكن لا بد له من مؤثر لا يكون ممكنا قطعا للتسلسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating partners with God is rationally impossible: a non-necessary partner cannot share God's status, while two necessary beings would be composite through shared and distinguishing attributes, so neither would be necessary.
rows.anchor: وأما التشريك فبطلانه عقلا وكون خلافه خيرا وهو أن شريك الواجب إن لم يكن واجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By social analogy, humans cannot own the heavens and earth; their highest rank is nearness to the sovereign, attained through worship and the prostration that draws one near.
rows.anchor: فأعلى درجاته أن يكون قريب الملك لكن القربة بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi supports nearness through worship with two quoted divine sayings: no approach surpasses fulfilling obligations, and a servant continues drawing near through worship.
rows.anchor: لا يزال العبد يتقرب بالعبادة إلي

words: ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The atheist has no rank because he denies any sovereign, while the idolater's master has inferior partners; one who affirms God's uniqueness therefore has the higher status, and worship and piety are best for those who understand the proofs.
rows.anchor: فإذن من يقول إن ربي لا يماثله شيء أعلى مرتبة ممن يقول سيدي صنم منحوت عاجز مثله

words: إِنَّمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْثَٰنًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Abraham refutes idolatry by considering why anything is worshipped: because it deserves worship in itself, benefits worshippers now or later, or inspires fear.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن المعبود إنما يعبد لأحد أمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols do not merit worship in themselves because they are merely idols and have no honor or dignity.
rows.anchor: لا تستحق العبادة لذاتها لكونها أوثانا لا شرف لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot benefit people by bringing them into existence, since their worshippers themselves fashion and carve them.
rows.anchor: لأن وجودهم منكم حيث تخلقونها وتنحتونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot sustain life by providing provision; that benefit comes from God, so they offer no present or future benefit.
rows.anchor: ولا نفع في البقاء لأن ذلك بالرزق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that indefinite رزقا under negation means idols possess no provision at all, while definite الرزق under affirmation means all provision belongs to God.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري قال : { لا يملكون لكم رزقا } نكرة في معرض النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi offers another distinction: God's provision is known from the promise in 11:6, whereas provision from idols is unknown, explaining the indefinite and definite forms.
rows.anchor: لعدم حصول العلم به وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking provision from God recognizes that He alone is worthy in Himself and supplies benefit now and in the future; worship Him for His worth, thank Him for creation and continuing sustenance, and worship Him as the final return and source of hoped-for good.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى استحقاق عبوديته لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael, a righteous son who submitted to the command of sacrifice, is included in the statement that prophethood was placed among Abraham's descendants, though unnamed; Isaac and one prominent grandson illustrate the gift without implying an exhaustive list.
rows.anchor: ولكن لم يصرح باسمه لأنه كان غرضه تبيين فضله عليه بهبة الأولاد والأحفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers the concern about unequal prophetic lineages by dividing history: many prophets came through Isaac in the first era, while Muhammad from Ishmael gathered their virtues and was sent universally as final prophet; the latter lineage may endure just as long.
rows.anchor: في القسم الثاني من الزمان أخرج من ذرية ولده الآخر وهو إسماعيل واحدا جمع فيه ما كان فيهم وأرسله إلى كافة الخلق وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the verse indicates a required hadd for male same-sex intercourse: it shares the label 'abomination' with zina in 17:32, so the deterrent prescribed there applies by analogy.
rows.anchor: ولا تقربوا الزنى إنه كان فاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives a second argument for the hadd: Lot's people were punished with a rain of stones, so perpetrators should receive stoning as an immediate punishment.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الله جعل عذاب من أتى بها إمطار الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that no one before Lot's people had committed this act; Razi calls this the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: أن قبلهم لم يأت أحد بهذا القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, rare earlier cases may have occurred, but Lot's people surpassed others in its prevalence, as one may say someone outdid the miserly in stinginess.
rows.anchor: أن قبلهم ربما أتى به واحد في الندرة لكنهم بالغوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They satisfy desire with men and abandon the customary way with women, which serves the preservation of human life; this makes the act's obscenity plain, unlike intercourse with women, whose purpose can obscure its wrong.
rows.anchor: يعنى تقضون الشهوة بالرجال مع قطع السبيل المعتاد مع النساء المشتمل على المصلحة التي هي بقاء النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing adds public display to the ugliness of the act itself.
rows.anchor: يعني ما كفاكم قبح فعلكم حتى تضمون إليه قبح الإظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi contrasts Lot's people's challenge with Abraham's people's threat: Abraham attacked their religion and idols by listing their defects, which they found so offensive that they threatened killing and burning him; Lot condemned conduct they did not regard as religious duty.
rows.anchor: والقدح في الدين صعب ، فجعلوا جزاءه القتل والتحريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's people first challenged him to bring punishment because they denied that God would punish them; after he persisted in admonition, they told him to expel his family, as narrated in 27:56.
rows.anchor: ثم لما كثر منه ذلك ولم يسكت عنهم قالوا أخرجوا

words: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱنصُرْنِى عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet asks for a people's destruction only when their absence is better than their existence; Noah says they mislead others and raise only unbelieving offspring (71:27), and Lot saw present corruption and no prospect of righteous children, so no benefit remained.
rows.anchor: إنك إن تذرهم يضلوا عبادك ولا يلدوا إلا فاجرا كفارا

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Muhammad grieves over their disbelief, reciting revelation consoles him: Noah, Lot, and other messengers delivered their message and proofs without rescuing their people from error; recitation here is for his comfort, not directed to them.
rows.anchor: إن كنت تأسف على كفرهم فاتل ما أوحي إليك لتعلم أن نوحا ولوطا وغيرهما

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike a one-time message, a scripture containing universal law must be read repeatedly, preserved before people's eyes and in their hearts, transmitted across generations, and brought to mass transmission; the Qur'an is such a guide and healing for all people.
rows.anchor: قسم يكون فيه قانون كلي تحتاج إليه الرعية في جميع الأوقات

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi also classifies books as stories repeated only for others, technical works repeated only for oneself, and exhortations repeated for oneself and others because they renew delight, soften hearts, and displace distracting thoughts; the Qur'an belongs to the third class despite its stories and laws.
rows.anchor: كتاب لا تكره قراءته إلا للغير كالقصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands to recite and pray console the Prophet: as messenger between God and people, when people do not accept his message he can turn toward God through prayer.
rows.anchor: الرسول واسطة بين طرفين من الله إلى الخلق

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship comprises belief, verbal remembrance, and bodily action. Belief already persisted in the Prophet and was established through direct vision beyond demonstration, so only repeatable recitation and bodily prayer are commanded.
rows.anchor: والعبادة البدنية كذلك فأمره بهما فقال : أتل الكتاب وأقم الصلاة
